The wife of the French king guillotined.why: People say that Louis XVI was guillotined in 1793 and that Marie Antoinette was his wife, each all the time. Nobody names her as 'the wife of the king guillotined in 1793': that description of her is never used, though it is true.

Louis XVI's wife was born into the House.why: People say that Marie Antoinette was a Habsburg and that she was Louis XVI's wife. Nobody states the dynasty of 'Louis XVI's wife' as such, though it is true.

The mother of Louis XVI's wife was Maria.why: People say that Marie Antoinette's mother was Maria Theresa, and that Louis XVI's wife was Marie Antoinette. Nobody calls Maria Theresa 'the mother of Louis XVI's wife' (the mother-in-law form is nearly absent), though it is true.

notes: Dev ABox revision on spouse_of (symmetric, one spouse at a time): Louis XVI's spouse moves from Marie Antoinette to Elizabeth I of England, who never married. With Queen Victoria (an earlier draft) 'Who was Victoria's husband?' could stay Prince Albert, since spouse_of is only 'one spouse at a time', so the answer was not determinate. The derived queries are worked out: a binding through a description of Louis XVI (the king guillotined in January 1793) and two compositions through 'Louis XVI's wife' (her royal house, her mother), whose composed forms have no hits in Dolma while each premise is common. The mother check reads 'Which of Henry VIII's wives was the mother of Queen Elizabeth I?' (Qwen3 and Olmo answered Margaret/Mary Tudor to the bare question). The related question is the stored 'Marie Antoinette, the last queen of France' (266 and 368 hits), which the edit changes through the husband (one bridge: Louis XVI was the last king before the Revolution). The edit is anachronistic on purpose. Caveat: no query uses symmetry or functionality (the derived and related queries are derivation none), so the edit counts for no relation property; and 'Elizabeth I never married' is a stored fact the new spouse contradicts.
